newsitem.title: FRANCE: MOTOR RACING-PROST THREATENS TO GIVE UP TEAM.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-PROST THREATENS TO GIVE UP TEAM.

text.p: Former world champion Alain Prost has threatened to give up his Formula One motor racing team because of bureaucratic hassles and political pressure.

"All I care for is to win. If I'm prevented from winning, I will draw all the necessary consequences," the Frenchman, head of the Prost Grand Prix team, told the French financial daily Les Echos on Thursday.
Prost said he was angered by the delayed transfer of his team's headquarters from Magny-Cours, site of the French Grand Prix for the past decade, to Versailles, near Paris.

The move set off a political controversy. The Magny-Cours area is dominated by the ruling Socialist party while the Versailles area is a traditional stronghold of the right, who support French president Jacques Chirac.
Magny-Cours, a small village near Nevers in central France, has been the home of the Ligier Formula One team which Prost bought back at the start of this season from Benetton chief Flavio Briatore.

"It was a businessman's decision (to leave Magny-Cours). Looking back, you'll realise Ligier were not efficient enough. It had nothing to do with their very competent staff but it was due to their isolation," Prost said.
He claimed the move from Magny-Cours to Versailles was blocked by an administrative committee in charge of helping firms settle in the French provinces.

The planting of Ligier's headquarters at Magny-Cours had received strong support from late French president Francois Mitterrand, who was first elected in the area and was a personal friend of team boss Guy Ligier.
Prost announced his team were moving to Versailles shortly before last June's general election in France. The transfer was seen in Magny-Cours as a political decision.
